plan: Reduce QQQI to 20% to lower concentration.
Exit all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU, METU) to zero.

Hold remaining broad index and quality tech positions.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation.

conservative.read: This plan focuses on capital preservation with a target of around 1.5% monthly return. It significantly reduces risk by cutting leveraged positions and holding a larger cash buffer. Expect lower volatility but also capped upside potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to manage concentration.
Reduce leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU, METU) to small positions.
Trim MSFU to reduce tech exposure.
Add XLF for sector diversification.
This plan balances risk reduction with growth opportunities.
Aims for steady, risk-managed returns.
balanced.read: This balanced approach targets approximately 2.5% monthly returns by managing risk first. It trims leveraged positions and adds diversification while maintaining some exposure to growth areas. Expect moderate growth with controlled drawdowns.

plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to manage concentration.
Increase leveraged tech ETFs (METU, SOXL, MUU, PLTU, SPAL, MSFU) to 6% each.

This plan aggressively pursues growth through leverage.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% monthly returns by leaning into leverage and concentration. It increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and high-scoring tech setups. Be aware of amplified gains, substantial drawdowns, and leveraged ETF decay. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Increase QQQI to 30% for income generation.
Exit all leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MUU, PLTU, SPAL) to zero.
Exit MSFU to reduce high-beta tech exposure.
Focus on steady monthly distributions.
This plan prioritizes income and capital preservation.
Expect low volatility and reliable income streams.
income.read: This income-focused plan targets around 1% monthly returns through distributions. It shifts the portfolio towards income-generating assets like QQQI and cuts all leveraged and high-beta positions. While prioritizing steady income, NAV can still decline in market selloffs.
